title: A higher-derivative model predicts a smoothness vs duration relationship in head-pointing movements
summary: Head movements require integration of visual, proprioceptive, vestibular, and cervical motor signals. The dynamical principles governing their temporal organization remain unclear. We tested whether a Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator -- a higher-derivative model with one internal frequency parameter $ω$ -- can model head kinematics during virtual-reality-based head pointing. Our model predicts a parabolic relationship between movement duration ($T$) and smoothness (log-dimensionless jerk, $LDLJ$) that we have experimentally checked.
